description:
TR: Göktürkler vizyonu, veri bilimiyle uzay araştırmalarına yön vermektir. "Serbest Düşüşte Alev" görevinde, mikro yerçekimi yanma verilerini yapay zekayla işleyip derin uzay görevleri için yenilikçi yangın güvenliği sistemleri geliştiriyoruz.

EN: Göktürkler's vision is to shape space exploration via data science. In "Flame in Freefall", we process microgravity combustion data with AI to build innovative fire safety systems for deep space missions.
summary:
PYROX is an autonomous, physics-informed microgravity fire diagnostic and suppression decision-support engine developed for spacecraft cabin safety. While existing orbital fire safety relies on passive smoke detection and manual, one-size-fits-all extinguishers, microgravity flames behave unpredictably—forming spherical diffusion envelopes, spreading strictly via HVAC airflow, and transitioning into invisible 500–800K "cool flames."

To address the "Flame in Freefall" challenge, we standardized 2,363 real ISS combustion and extinction tests from 14 NASA PSI datasets (including FLEX, CFI, CFI-G, BASS-II, and SAFFIRE). PYROX operates through a unified 3-Core Hybrid Pipeline: Core-1 (Gas) and Core-2 (Solid/Polymer) calculate thermodynamic features—Stoichiometric Mixture Fraction (Zst), Adiabatic Flame Temperature (Tad), Limiting Oxygen Index (LOI), and Flame Spread Rate (Vf)—to diagnose fire severity. Core-3 then simulates six suppression strategies (CO₂, Helium, N₂, Partial Vacuum, HVAC Cutoff, and Blow-off) across a 24-sector (6×4) cellular automaton cabin map in 3 milliseconds. Every decision is scientifically validated against real ISS flight tests via 4D Euclidean k-NN matching, preventing cool-flame reignition and protecting crewed Artemis and Mars missions.
details:
LIVE DEMO & SIMULATION CONSOLE: https://pyrox.quasacode.com/

1. WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS (3-Core Physics-Informed Architecture)

PYROX (Physical Yield & Real-time Oxygen X-tinction Engine) is an autonomous microgravity fire diagnostic and suppression decision-support system. Instead of relying on a single black-box model, PYROX processes 2,363 standardized ISS flight test records from 14 NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) datasets through a two-stage, 3-Core Hybrid Pipeline:

• Thermodynamic Pre-Computation Layer: Raw cabin telemetry (Pressure P, Oxygen Mole Fraction XO₂, and HVAC Flow Velocity) is insufficient to capture combustion chemistry. Before inference, PYROX computes three physics-informed features: Stoichiometric Mixture Fraction (Zst), Adiabatic Flame Temperature (Tad) adjusted for diluent molar heat capacity (Cp), and Dynamic Limiting Oxygen Index (LOI) alongside microgravity Flame Spread Rate (Vf in mm/s).

• Stage 1 — Phase-Specific Diagnosis (Core-1 & Core-2): Core-1 (trained on 1,087 gas tests from CFI-G, SPICE, s-Flame, Flame Design) and Core-2 (trained on 307 solid/polymer tests from BASS-II, SAFFIRE) diagnose unmitigated peak burner temperature (°C), critical LOI thresholds, and real-time flame spread rate (Vf).

• Stage 2 — Autonomous Suppression Optimization (Core-3): Powered by 969 extinction tests (FLEX, FLEX-2, CFI, BASS-II), Core-3 takes the thermal severity and cabin spread ratio (%spread) to simultaneously simulate 6 suppression strategies in a 6×7 batch matrix within ~3 milliseconds:

1) CO₂ Injection (NOZ-1 - High molar heat capacity radical quenching)

2) Helium Thermal Quenching (NOZ-2 - High thermal conductivity heat dissipation)

3) Standard N₂ Dilution (NOZ-3 - Oxygen displacement below LOI)

4) Partial Vacuum Depressurization + N₂ (0.50 bar rapid partial-pressure drop)

5) HVAC Fan Cutoff (0 cm/s starvation of convective O₂ transport)

6) High-Velocity Fan Blow-off (45 cm/s strain-rate detachment for small local flames)

2. HOW OUR PROJECT IS CREATIVE & INNOVATIVE

• From Passive Prediction to Prescriptive Control: Most solutions only predict whether a fuel will burn. PYROX acts as an active flight-control advisor that ranks suppression methods by efficiency (%) and estimated extinction time (s).

• Dual-Canvas Real-Time Simulation: Our web console features two synchronized HTML5 Canvas engines: a Micro-Scale Combustion Chamber (side view showing spherical diffusion flames, HVAC fan dynamics, and 3 independent dedicated nozzles: NOZ-1 [CO₂], NOZ-2 [He], NOZ-3 [N₂]) and a Macro-Scale 24-Sector (6×4) Cellular Automaton Cabin Map (top-down view modeling elliptical flame front propagation and perimeter gas inerting).

• Zero-Hallucination Scientific Proof (4D Euclidean k-NN): To prove the AI is not fabricating recommendations, every decision is paired with a 4-dimensional Euclidean k-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN) matcher that retrieves the 5 closest real NASA ISS experiments (with exact PSI codes, test IDs, and similarity percentages).

3. KEY FACTORS OUR TEAM CONSIDERED

• The "Spread Ratio Paradox": In microgravity, natural buoyancy is absent; flames rely on HVAC ventilation for fresh O₂. Our team modeled a critical operational threshold: when cabin fire spread is below 20%, high-velocity airflow (45 cm/s Blow-off) can detach and extinguish a small flame. However, once spread exceeds 25%, blowing air fans the fire into a cabin-wide furnace. PYROX automatically penalizes blow-off above 25% spread and shifts priority to HVAC Cutoff, CO₂, or Partial Vacuum.

• 500–800K Invisible "Cool Flame" Reignition: Heavy hydrocarbons (n-Heptane, n-Dodecane, Butane) transition into invisible cool flames after visible extinction. PYROX detects cool-flame risk and locks suppressant dosing above the radical-quenching threshold (≥35% concentration) to prevent explosive reignition.

• Dedicated 3-Nozzle Manifold Realism: To prevent cross-gas contamination and valve deadlocks, we designed three independent nozzle lines for CO₂, He, and N₂.

4. BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT

• Empirical Superiority: Analysis of NASA PSI data through PYROX demonstrates that shutting off HVAC flow in solid fires (BASS-II) achieves 100% extinction in 5.5s on average, compared to 22.0s (16.4% success) with standard N₂ flooding. Similarly, He and CO₂ reduce gas and droplet extinction times by 60–70% compared to N₂.

• Mission Readiness for Artemis & Mars: By compressing 6-strategy evaluation into 3 milliseconds via batch vectorization (a 30x speedup), PYROX is lightweight enough to be embedded directly into Environmental Control and Life Support Systems (ECLSS) on the ISS, Lunar Gateway, and deep-space habitats.

5. TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES & SOFTWARE USED

• Backend & Machine Learning: Python 3, FastAPI, Scikit-Learn (HistGradientBoostingClassifier, HistGradientBoostingRegressor, RandomForest, NearestNeighbors, StandardScaler), Pandas, NumPy, Joblib, Pydantic, Uvicorn, and a2wsgi.

• Frontend & Visualization: HTML5, CSS3 / TailwindCSS, Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+), Dual HTML5 2D Canvas Physics & Cellular Automaton Rendering Engine, Fetch API with AbortController concurrency management.

• Deployment: Hosted live on Linux cPanel production environment at https://pyrox.quasacode.com/
